column2: State what students are expected to learn, understand, or be able to do by the end of the lesson. This should clearly describe the focus of the learning and be aligned with curriculum goals, helping to provide direction and purpose for both teaching and learning.

Define the specific, observable indicators that demonstrate successful achievement of the learning intention. These criteria guide students in understanding what success looks like and support teachers in assessing learning. Where appropriate, use “I can” statements to make criteria student-friendly.

Outline the step-by-step flow of the lesson, including key stages such as introduction, teaching, guided practice, independent tasks, and conclusion. This sequence should reflect how learning will be scaffolded and paced to ensure clarity, engagement, and progression.

Describe the strategies used to meet the diverse learning needs, abilities, and interests of students. This may include adjustments to content, process, product, or learning environment, and should ensure all students are appropriately supported and challenged.

List all materials, tools, digital resources, and teaching aids required to deliver the lesson effectively. Include specific items such as worksheets, manipulatives, technology, texts, or visual aids to ensure readiness and smooth lesson implementation.
